profile.headline: Software Engineer III at Framatome | Founder at Aski | AI & Software Innovation
profile.summary:
I'm a software engineer and founder passionate about building AI powered products that solve real world business challenges.

My experience spans AI, software engineering, cloud technologies, and product development, with a focus on transforming complex operational workflows into intuitive, scalable solutions. I enjoy working across the entire product lifecycle, from identifying customer problems and defining product strategy to delivering solutions that create measurable business value.

I founded Aski, a hospitality operations platform that helps hotels streamline daily operations through intelligent workflows, task management, maintenance coordination, scheduling, and team communication.

I'm particularly interested in applied AI, workflow automation, SaaS platforms, and building products that improve operational efficiency across industries. I enjoy collaborating with cross functional teams, learning from customers, and turning innovative ideas into practical solutions.

I'm always interested in connecting with professionals who are passionate about AI, software engineering, product innovation, and digital transformation.

projects.title: Low-Cost LiDAR Scanner
projects.description:
Biomechanics is a field which requires extensive analysis of animals before adapting them into robotic platforms. Providing a depth image of an animal allows one to configure and construct joints and muscle placements to further analyse how they operate and function together. Conventional depth cameras require multiple angles to accurately provide depth or require markers on animals to map depth. LiDAR is an approach to provide depth of an animal using a single sensor. Conventional lidar scanners take a long time to scan an area and are very costly. This research intends to develop a low-cost lidar system that could reduce the time taken for scans but ensure enough data points have been collected for a high resolution depth image.
Initial research was done in order to gain understanding of how depth cameras produce 3D images and what requirements the LiDAR system needed to fulfil. Thereafter the concept of LiDAR was researched and how the technology would be used to gather point cloud data. A design approach was implemented to provide multiple axis rotation and present spherical system data coordinates which would then be processed into a depth image. Multiple tests were performed for verification of depth and positioning along with optimisation for reduced scanning time and better resolution.
Data was further processed and critically analysed for improvements in the applied algorithms and implemented functions. The results showed a successful project where the LiDAR scanner was able to replicate a human subject in a 3D environment.
